newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline up partly on IPL outage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline up partly on IPL outage.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent oil products generally firmed Monday, with gasoline getting a boost from potential refinery disruptions caused by a halt to throughput on Canada's Interprovincial crude pipeline.

Outright gasoline prices were also boosted by a bounce in futures prices in New York, where May rose 0.25 cent to 60.72 cents a gallon. But gasoline and heating oil fell from their highs and May heating oil ended off 0.02 at 53.12 cents.
"Gasoline is up three-quarters in the Group," said a dealer at a major trading house, referring to the higher premium over futures for physical gasoline in Group Three.

Part of the IPL crude pipeline, which supplies about 1.4 million barrels a day to midwestern U.S. refiners, was shut from late Saturday evening as a number of pumping stations in Minnesota were knocked out by a power outage there.
Market players differed over the likely effect of the pipeline disruption, though there was general agreement that it would depend how long the line remained down.

Refineries in the large states around the Great Lakes account for about 2.3 million barrels a day of crude processing, or about 15 percent of the U.S. total. There may also be a displacement effect if refineries in Ontario, Canada side of the border.

The Koch refinery in Minnesota, with 286,000 bpd of crude distillation capacity, said Monday it was running on inventories and expected no short-term impact, though couldn't say how the market might be affected if there is a prolonged outage.
Other large refineries in the region, like Amoco, Mobil, Shell and Ashland, may find it easier to secure alternative crude from the south where there is a glut.
Meanwhile, prompt Chicago unleaded was up 0.50 to 0.75 cents, about half of which was an improvement in the differential. Group Three unleaded was bid 2.0 cents a gallon under for all April timings.
